items.subject: Faith
items.summary: Elder Austin Nelson shared his weekly mission update, a favorite verse, a long bike ride, and a phone prank in Mamelodi.
items.body:
I think my favorite verse this week was Proverbs 3:5-6. Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

What hapened this week
This week thursday we decided to go by bike. Our last lesson canceled and we had a bit of time. At this point we were clear across town. We decided extra time means extra contacting. So we decided to try to bike back to the church on our own without using maps, just the spirit. We biked for a long time talking to people along the way. Suddenly we notice it's getting dim. At this point we finally give in and use maps. I think the spirit told us to. We navigate to the church only to find ourselves 20 miles away. We peddled hard! It was a successful trip we found a few interested people and a lottt of drunk people.

I think the funnest moment this week was Saturday. We were in the heart of the Mamelodi township contacting in public when we run into a bar. This bar comes out after us. It was overwhelming with so many crazys. These guys are asking what the heck we are doing in a township. White people are not in there natural habitat here. After talking to them about 5 minutes I realized my phone was not in my pocket. I felt dumb to have my phone just disappeared like that. My companion, and Owabile a member of the ward were still caught up in conversation with others. Me just thinking i want out of here. But yet still i was answering questions. As we finially start pulling away from this group one of the guys runs and buys us ice-cream. We except cautiously but thank him. When I finially got a chance to talk to my companion I tell him that my phone was snatched. He then said "I got mine" reaches in his pocket and pulls out my phone. It was so funny.

Mirical of the week, free ice cream
(Maximum rating 2/10)

Make sure to trust in the Lord
-Elder Nelson

items.subject: Halloween and Día de los Muertos
items.summary: Sister Heintzelman's weekly mission letter from south Texas about Halloween, Día de los Muertos, and her last weeks serving.
items.body:
What is up y'all? The good news is that the Gospel of Jesus Christ is alive and well. Setting hearts on fire all across south Texas. Qué bendición!

For starters we had an awesome p-day playing sports as a district and we all got sunburned. (Still worth it.) And as always the best talks with my family.

Guys...we found a family! This is amazing, and almost never happens in our work. But the Lord was working His miracles. Because of a few scheduling mishaps we had the opportunity to go knock this door one last time. And we found Neydy and Gabriel and their sweet little kids. They were so cute and running around everywhere. And the parents were super interested in learning more. Please pray for them!

Wednesday was our temple day and it was so calming as always. The Lord knew what He was doing putting me in missions with temples close by. He knew I would need them.

Thursday was a wild ride but it included an awesome lesson with Anika, Aida and then later Brenda. And we had a Relief Society Activity where we had quite a few friends show up and we celebrated Ruby and Margie as our two strong cancer survivors. Ruby was quite proud of herself.

I can't believe another Halloween has already passed. And with that I got my first Día de los Muertos. For any of you that don't know what that is, watch Coco and it will explain it better than I can. But it is a beautiful celebration of life and ancestors that is very prominent in Mexico. We even had a giant ofrenda at our combined ward party and a bunch of people brought the photos of their departed family members. Speaking of which a bunch of friends came to the party, and a few that we weren't expecting which was AWESOME.

This week also held a lot of lasts. My last MLC, interview with Presidente, holiday on the mission. And I can't believe I am saying this but I had my last fast and testimony meeting of my mission yesterday. It was quite bittersweet and yet wonderful. Safe to say there were many tears shed between me and the branch. But what a blessing it has been to share 11 months with these people. I don't think I could ever forget even one of them.

Priesthood power. One of the most awe-inspiring and majestic truths of this day. We have the literal and true power of God on the earth again. The power to perform ordinances and make Covenants through the name and power of Christ. How incredible is that? I know in many ways I take this for granted but I want to testify of this power. Especially priesthood blessings. That God is opening heaven and literally connecting us back to Him through His power. The same miracles of old are given to us through His servants here. Of peace, comfort, and healing. I'll let you in on a little secret, missions are a lot of work and many times they can be difficult. But the Lord will always provide a way that we may accomplish His work. (1 Nephi 3:7) Every single one of us has access to His priesthood power through our obedience and faithfulness. Never forget that He is walking this road with you. He is the God of our salvation, our strength, and our song. The one who calms the storms and heals the broken hearts. Of this I testify in the name of Jesus Christ amen.

I am praying for all of you, especially my fellow missionaries. May God be with you all til we meet again.

Sister Heintzelman 🤟🏼

items.subject: 🎵Baby I know that you like mee🎶 - Soulja Boy
items.summary: Brysen's weekly mission letter shares a funny exchange story and a spiritual thought about God's timing in teaching Francis.
items.body:
I may have involuntary found my eternal companion (for the next 2 years).
So basically I was on another exchange and this lady starts calling out to me saying how im gonna be the father for her next kids, then was asking me if I like her. (She looks like she's jn her 40s btw). Then she said she was gonna follow me to America when I leave. Ladies, yall got some real competition

This week was pretty uneventful other than that. Except, for the event that leads to thus weeks

Spiritual thought:

When teaching lessons usually you dk them jn the order kf teach the restoration first, then the plan of Salvation, then the gospel of Jesus christ (4th article of faith basicalky), then all the nitty gritty stuff. But for some reason when we were teaching this guy named francis we started the plan kf salvation, we didnt teach the full thing. We talked about the premortal life, the creation, and the fall of Adam and eve, then the next day we skipped the rest and went to the gospel of Jesus christ.

Last time when we met with him, I was looking at the lesson plan and was thinking "why did we skip that part?" Only to find out that his uncle just died and he was torn about it. We then taught him the rest of the plan of Salvation, and i could see his attitude start to change as we started to talk about ghe spirit world Nd how we will rest frkm our troubles there. Comparing him before and after fhe lesson, you could see a new light in his mind.

That my friends, is why. Why we skipped over it before. Because gods timing is perfect. Because god knew he needed that portion of the lesson at that time.

We definitely will be questioning why some things played out how they did, but just remember, gods plan is perfect.

Sp whatever happens just remember that

Have a great week fellas!!!!
